items.title: Retrieving from Your Own Mistakes: On-Policy Training of Embedding Models for Multi-Hop Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.summary_1line: Complex questions in retrieval-augmented generation require evidence spread over several documents, and an answer is reliable only when the retriever finds all of it. Chain embedding retrievers collect such evidence s...
items.editor_note: Targets multi-hop RAG by training the embedding retriever on its own failures.

items.title: TRIO: Task Refinement with Individual Optimization for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.summary_1line: This paper studies retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), which leverages external knowledge to improve the performance of language models. Despite the remarkable progress, current RAG approaches are still far from sat...
items.editor_note: Frames current RAG as unsatisfactory and proposes TRIO for task refinement.

items.title: Assessing the Impact of Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Algorithmic Problem-Solving

items.title: Compaction, decay and reinforcement in a two-tier conversational memory: a paired evaluation against retrieval-augmented generation

items.title: OpticalRAG: Pixel-Space Compression for Token-Efficient Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.summary_1line: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is bottlenecked by the token budget of large language models: feeding long documents into the context window is expensive, while aggressive textual compression discards fine-graine...
items.editor_note: Adds the cost angle: pixel-space compression to fit long documents in the token budget.

items.title: Cited but Unused: Parametric Provenance in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.summary_1line: Retrieval-augmented generation systems attach citations to attribute claims to their sources. These citations frequently misstate provenance, and standard verification cannot detect this. We measure provenance by coun...
items.editor_note: First item in the thread to question RAG's citations: attached sources may not be what the model used.

editorial.tldr: Late-October and early-November papers worked on the RAG pipeline itself: training embedding retrievers on their own mistakes for multi-hop questions, and TRIO's task refinement. By Nov 6-10 the papers were testing RAG's assumptions instead, against compacted fact memory, on competitive programming, and against the context token budget.
editorial.whats_new: A Nov 12 paper, "Cited but Unused," reports that RAG citations frequently misstate where an answer came from, and that standard citation verification cannot detect it.
editorial.why_it_matters: A citation that passes verification may still not be what the model used, so citation checks alone do not prove a RAG answer is grounded in the retrieved documents.
editorial.take_for_builders: If you treat citations as your groundedness signal, add an ablation check to your evals: remove the cited passage and see whether the answer changes.

status.detail: Six separate arXiv papers in two weeks, not one event: they probe retriever training, pipeline refinement, agent memory, code tasks, context cost, and citation provenance.

beats.headline: Training embedding models on their own retrieval mistakes for multi-hop RAG
beats.summary: Multi-hop answers are only reliable if the retriever finds all the evidence.

beats.headline: TRIO proposes task refinement with individual optimization for RAG
RAG measured against compacted fact memory and on competitive programming
beats.summary: Two Nov 6 papers evaluate where RAG helps instead of proposing a new retriever.

beats.headline: OpticalRAG compresses retrieved documents in pixel space to save tokens
beats.summary: It targets the token budget, arguing aggressive text compression discards fine-grained detail.

beats.headline: "Cited but Unused": RAG citations frequently misstate provenance
beats.summary: The paper says standard verification cannot detect the mismatch.

open_questions: Do the multi-hop retriever gains hold on benchmarks other than those the paper reports?
Does compacted fact memory beat transcript RAG outside the paper's paired evaluation?
Will any of these methods ship in a widely used RAG framework?
Does the citation-provenance gap reproduce across models and RAG stacks beyond those the paper measured?
Does a practical check emerge that catches a cited-but-unused source in production?
Does pixel-space compression preserve answer accuracy on documents where exact figures or identifiers matter?
